chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Ismail ibn al-Fadl said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about selling the fruit before it is ripe, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is such that in that land, selling it is [like selling] a crop which has ripened, then selling all of that is permissible.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell fruit before it ripens according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility of selling unripe fruit by invoking the principle of 'urf' (local custom), ruling that if a specific crop is traditionally traded in its current state of development within that region, the sale is valid. This hadith highlights the Shia juristic reliance on customary practice to determine the validity of conditional sales, distinguishing between the intrinsic nature of the fruit and the local market norms. It underscores the flexibility of Islamic commercial law in accommodating regional agricultural practices.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from someone else, from Ismail Bin Al Fazl who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about selling the fruits before they ripen, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was such that in that particular land, selling of it is (like selling) a crop which has ripened, so selling all of that is Permissible’.
en.sarwar: 6. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama’ah from more than one person from ‘Isma’il ibn al-Fadl who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam) about selling fruits. ‘Is it permissible to buy fruits before they are formed?’
He (the Imam) replied, ‘If in that area such deals are made and they are profitable which is achieved then there is no offense in such transaction.’”
